A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ExpertAF. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: V1 reports original commentary-generation, demonstration-retrieval and pose-generation experiments, ablations and human evaluations in Table 1 and the appendix.

after.justification: V2 reports these original experiments and human evaluations, together with additional model, training and input-view ablations in supplementary Table 2.

M1.justification: The dataset-mining pipeline, temporal alignment, modality tokenizers and training objectives are retained. V2 clarifies learner-only inference and relabels existing input variants. Log-likelihood retrieval scoring was already documented in v1 Appendix A.3; the revised explanation does not establish a new retrieval method.

E1.justification: Both versions use Ego-Exo4D basketball, soccer and rock climbing for the same three feedback tasks. The added model and view ablations use retained data coverage rather than introducing another dataset, population or task.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains InternVideo2-NN-train as InternVideo2-NN, removes InternVideo2-NN-test and adds contrastively fine-tuned InternVideo2-FT. VideoChat2, LLaVA and its fine-tuned variants, and PoseScript/Fix remain evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: V2 adds Llama3.2 1B/3B configurations, separate versus joint sport training, and ego/exo input controls. It makes the already-tested learner-only setting primary and explicitly separates privileged-input full-sup evaluation. Dataset splits, metrics, stated training schedules and human-study sampling remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Supplementary Section D and Table 2 add systematic analyses of language-model capacity, cross-scenario training, individual camera views and pose compensation for missing exocentric video. These substantially expand the diagnostic evidence beyond v1's modality, alignment, global-pose and input-supervision ablations. Figure 4 also revises qualitative cases.

E5.justification: V2 removes v1's five-generation statement and aggregate standard-deviation bounds: within 0.1 for commentary metrics and recall, within 2 for median rank, and below 3 mm for pose error. No replacement uncertainty estimates appear. This establishes reduced reporting, not fewer actual repetitions.

E6.justification: V2 adds six supplementary ablation result rows and InternVideo2-FT results, and revises existing ablation scores, human ratings and Figure 4 examples. The old primary and incorrect-only result vectors are retained as full-sup and default respectively; their relabeling is not a same-setting performance decline.

T1.justification: V2's unified F/F-prime notation and numbered inference equations reorganize the existing formulation. The pairing rule, temporal-alignment minimization and cross-entropy objectives are retained. Neither version contains additional theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: V2 removes v1's explicit first-of-its-kind expert-pose-generation claim, describing a novel technique instead. The broader claims of introducing actionable video coaching, constructing a weakly supervised dataset and outperforming the evaluated baselines remain.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the new ablations through language-model strength, cross-scenario learning and pose compensation for missing exocentric views. Existing pose-noise, feedback-granularity and visually ungrounded-feedback limitations remain, while v1 Appendix A.6's societal-impact and population-bias discussion is removed.

D1.justification: V2 specifies Llama3-70B for commentary preprocessing, Llama3-8B for sequence prediction and the same text backbone for fine-tuned LLaVA baselines. It also explicitly states the 1,272-item retrieval pool. These are additional disclosures; hardware, frame sampling and promised code/data release remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations to Maluleke et al., Zhang et al. and Vaswani, and contrasts its pose-token approach with pose regression and dedicated motion Transformers. It removes the Carreira et al. and Zhao et al. pose-feedback references. The overall related-work coverage remains similar.

P1.justification: V2 substantially rewrites the problem statement and training-versus-inference explanation, reorganizes the results narrative around default and full-sup variants, and restructures the appendix into separate lettered sections. Wording and body-part/body-region terminology are revised throughout.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column layout. Table 1 separates automatic scores from human-rating bar charts, Table 2 is added, and multiple figures are rearranged or redesigned with colored panels, clearer labels and correction annotations.

improvement.justification: V2 more clearly distinguishes learner-only inference from privileged-input evaluation and adds useful evidence about model capacity, joint training and camera-view contributions. These improve interpretability and experimental support. The gain is limited because learner-only results already existed in v1, while v2 drops its uncertainty disclosures; the revision does not establish a same-setting performance improvement.
